tagline: A southern border town on the Andaman, a UNESCO Global Geopark, the Tarutao–Koh Lipe islands, and a quiet Muslim way of life
introHtml:
Satun is the southernmost Andaman province, right on the Malaysian border. Most people picture it through its clear-water islands like Koh Lipe and Koh Tarutao, and through the fact that the whole province is a UNESCO Global Geopark, with caves, limestone mountains, and fossils hundreds of millions of years old you can actually go and see. It's a small town that moves slowly and still isn't as busy as Thailand's other beach provinces.

In town you'll find the old Kuden Mansion, the Mambang Mosque, and Muslim food markets. People who love nature take boats out to the islands, kayak into Lay Stegodon Cave, or cruise around Pak Bara and the Andaman bays. The food here is bold southern Thai cooking with a Malay accent — roti, gaeng tai pla, and khao yam. People come to Satun for clear seas, quiet islands, and limestone scenery you don't see in many places.
bestTime: November–April, when the skies clear and the sea is calm and clear, ideal for island-hopping and diving. Many places on Koh Lipe close during the May–October monsoon.

highlights.name: Koh Lipe
highlights.blurb: The small, clear-water island that's Satun's main draw, with white-sand beaches like Sunrise Beach and Pattaya Beach, a walking street through the middle of the island, and snorkeling spots all around. It's the image that comes to mind the moment anyone mentions this province.

highlights.name: Tarutao National Park
highlights.blurb: A cluster of islands in the middle of the Andaman that was once an old prison, with Pante Malacca Bay, white-sand beaches, and rainforest on the islands. Take a boat from Pak Bara and you can sightsee and see the prison history in a single day.

highlights.name: Satun Global Geopark
highlights.blurb: The whole province is listed as a UNESCO Global Geopark, thanks to its limestone, caves, and ancient marine fossils hundreds of millions of years old. It's a geological story that sets Satun apart from the usual beach town.

highlights.name: Lay Stegodon Cave
highlights.blurb: A water cave you kayak through, deep into the dark for several kilometres. A Stegodon elephant fossil was found inside, and it's the geopark's best-known cave trip.

highlights.name: Pak Bara
highlights.blurb: Satun's main pier and the jump-off point for boats to Tarutao, Koh Lipe, and the islands around them, with a beach, a market, and seafood restaurants by the water. It's the staging area before you board for the islands.

highlights.name: Old town and Muslim culture
highlights.blurb: Downtown Satun has the Kuden Mansion, the Mambang Mosque, and Muslim food markets, reflecting a deep-south way of life touched by Malay culture. It's easy to stroll past the old buildings and try the local food.

foodScene.name: Andaman seafood
foodScene.note: On the coast and with its own fishing boats, you get fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish. Seafood spots at Pak Bara and in town do it grilled, steamed, stir-fried with curry powder, and in tom yum.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, yellow curry, khua kling, and stir-fried sator with shrimp, eaten with hot rice and fresh raw vegetables. It's the local home-style meal you can find all over town.

foodScene.name: Southern khao yam
foodScene.note: Rice tossed with budu sauce, shredded vegetables, toasted coconut, and dried shrimp — sour, salty, and sweet in one plate. It's a light breakfast Satun locals eat all the time.

foodScene.name: Roti and cha chak at Muslim shops
foodScene.note: Satun is a Muslim town, and roti and cha chak shops are open from morning till late. Roti is crisp outside and soft inside, eaten with curry or drizzled with sweet milk, with hot pulled tea for breakfast and snacks.

foodScene.name: Nasi dagae and Malay rice curry
foodScene.note: Rice wrapped in banana leaf topped with southern-Malay curry, eaten with boiled egg and fish. It's a quick breakfast sold at markets and tea shops in town.

foodScene.name: Southern khanom jeen nam ya
foodScene.note: Fresh rice noodles in bold southern nam ya curry, eaten with all kinds of raw vegetables, from yardlong beans to cashew shoots. Khanom jeen shops open early in the morning.

foodScene.name: Seafood by the Pak Bara pier
foodScene.note: Restaurants by the pier cook seafood fresh off the fishing boats — fried fish, stir-fried shellfish, and grilled shrimp. You can sit and watch the boats before or after heading out to the islands.

foodScene.name: Cafés and coffee in town
foodScene.note: Around town and on Koh Lipe there are new cafés brewing fresh coffee and making local sweets. They're an easy place to stop and sip a coffee during the day.

attractions.name: Koh Lipe
attractions.blurb: A clear-water island with Sunrise Beach, Pattaya Beach, and snorkeling spots all around, plus a walking street through the middle for food and shopping. It's great for an easygoing stay of several nights.

attractions.name: Tarutao National Park
attractions.blurb: A cluster of islands in the middle of the Andaman with Pante Malacca Bay, white-sand beaches, rainforest, and traces of the old prison. Take a boat from Pak Bara for a day trip or an overnight stay.

attractions.name: Lay Stegodon Cave
attractions.blurb: A water cave you kayak into, deep in the dark for several kilometres, where a Stegodon elephant fossil was once found. It's the standout cave trip of the Satun Global Geopark.

attractions.name: Khao Pan Yod stone castle
attractions.blurb: A limestone island with sharp, castle-like spires rising from the sea. Slip inside the small lagoon ringed by stalactites and stalagmites — an unusual photo spot within the geopark.

attractions.name: Wang Sai Thong Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tiered limestone waterfall whose water runs over wide rock terraces, clear and cool. A short walk gets you in to swim and picnic by the falls — a popular nature spot in the province.

attractions.name: Kuden Mansion
attractions.blurb: An old building of mixed European and Malay architecture that was once the Satun governor's residence. Today it's a museum telling the town's history and local way of life, and a landmark in the centre of town.

attractions.name: Satun Central Mosque (Mambang)
attractions.blurb: The provincial mosque at the heart of Satun's Muslim community, with handsome architecture in the middle of town, reflecting the faith and culture that anchor the province.

attractions.name: Koh Hin Ngam
attractions.blurb: A small island in the Tarutao area covered with round, glossy black stones lining the beach. People stop to walk and take photos during island tours — an unusual spot that always draws a crowd.

itineraryIdeas: Satun 2D1N — Pak Bara, Tarutao, and Koh Lipe
Satun island run — Koh Lipe, snorkeling, and an overnight stay on the island
Satun nature route — Lay Stegodon Cave, Khao Pan Yod stone castle, and Wang Sai Thong Waterfall
Satun town and culture — Kuden Mansion, Mambang Mosque, and the Muslim market
Satun–Trang — along the Andaman, islands and caves across two provinces
Satun–Songkhla — cross the deep-south border for beaches on both coasts
